title: Owatonna Symphony Orchestra performing this weekend with over 200 musicians - NewsBreak
text:
Owatonna
Owatonna Symphony Orchestra performing this weekend with over 200 musicians
By LIZZIE COOPER,
11 hours agoThis local orchestra is bringing the experience of a symphony concert to the people of Owatonna this weekend and it’s entirely free to attend.
The Owatonna Symphony Orchestra is proud to announce its second annual Fall Concert at 3 p.m. on Oct. 12 at St. John Lutheran Church. The program is titled “Beethoven, the Beatles and All That Jazz.”
The program is a collection of favorite tunes from classical to pop to jazz. Selections such as Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony, “Hoedown” from Rodeo and music from the movie “E.T.” are balanced with Beatles’ favorites and the best of Duke Ellington.
“There’s going to be some classical, some pop music, and even some movie music,” said Philip Burkhart, the orchestra’s co-director.
Burkhart said the point of the concert is to get people to come to a symphony concert. Through offering a variety of music, the setlist should appeal to everyone regardless of age or musical experience.
“Our original thought was to do it to attract people, all kinds of people, to a symphony concert. That’s why we chose music from all kinds of different areas,” Burkhart said.
The Owatonna Symphony has also invited all 112 string players from Owatonna High School to join their performance for one piece. For this piece, over 200 musicians will be performing simultaneously inside the church. The musicians will surround the audience with this piece, lining the walls of the church with their performance.
According to Burkhart, Owatonna’s band, choir and orchestra programs are some of the best not only in Minnesota, but in the Midwest.
“They are highly respected for their level of playing,” Burkhart said.
When he first visited Owatonna in 1982, Burkhart noticed the quality of Owatonna’s music programs and said it has been maintained throughout the years.
“I want the community of Owatonna to hear these kids play,” Burkhart said.
About the orchestra
The Owatonna Symphony Orchestra is a community orchestra primarily composed of adults, although there are a few students amongst the musicians as well. This musical group has players from as far as Mankato, Minneapolis, Rochester and Austin with the majority of players from the Owatonna community.
A total of two concerts a year are performed by this community orchestra, and they are completely free for the public to attend, with encouragement to support the program through donations.
All of the musicians playing in the Owatonna Symphony Orchestra voluntarily practice and perform for the love of the music.
“These musicians come from all walks of life,” Burkhart said.
Many of the musicians are teachers, medical professionals, salesmen, housewives or from other occupations. This is a group of adults who played earlier in their lives and wanted to get together to play again, according to Burkhart.
Burkhart has been living in Austin for 43 years and taught string music there for 30 years before retiring. Now, he goes around to different schools, working with the orchestras there. He said he either judges them for solo ensemble or large group contests, along with helping out school orchestras when the directors ask him to.
“I’ve been coming to Owatonna and working with these groups for at least 10 years, and so I have a connection. I know the directors personally. They’re good friends of mine and they ask me to come up and work with their groups,” Burkhart explained.
Peter Guenther, the band director at OHS, directs the spring concerts. Through his connection to the school district, Burkhart got to know Guenther. Once the Owatonna Symphony Orchestra decided to start performing two concerts a year, Guenther asked Burkhart to direct the fall concert due to the peak of marching band season occurring around the same time.
“I jumped on it, because I love doing it,” Burkhart said.
The spring concerts held by OSO have more classical setlists, but the performances are still entirely free for the public to attend. The coming spring concert in April will be patriotic-themed, celebrating America’s 250th anniversary.
